newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland says flood relief bonds considered for 1998.
newsitem.headline: Poland says flood relief bonds considered for 1998.

text.p: The Polish government will consider issuing special bonds next year to raise funds for the reconstruction of areas ravaged by July's catastrophic floods, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Monday.

Poland's biggest opposition group, the Solidarity Election Action (AWS), proposed last week that the bonds, which are to be deducted from personal income tax, be launched this year. Cimoszewicz rejected that plan.

"At the moment we see no urgent need of gathering additional means to finance these activities (reconstructing the flooded regions)," he told reporters after a meeting of the government's National Programme of Reconstruction and Modernisation Council.

"We have considered...the flood bonds... They could be used if, during works on (next year's) budget draft, it turns out that it is necessary to supplement the sources of financing the reconstruction," Cimoszewicz said.
According to independent analysts the floods -- which killed 55 people while destroying many roads, bridges and buildings -- caused damages of up to 7.5 billion zlotys.

The government has earmarked some 650 million zlotys for flood relief which it squeezed from this year's budget. It also plans to borrow about $600 million from the World Bank and the European Investment Bank (EIB).

As an emergency measure, parliament has authorised the government to borrow an additioanl 2.5 billion zlotys ($728 million) from the National Bank of Poland this year, of which one billion zlotys has already been drawn.

The AWS, which is the main challenger of Cimoszewicz's ex-communist party in parliamentary elections on September 21, has said the goverment plan to borrow money from the central bank would stir inflation.

"Issuing the flood bonds would help avoid more inflation," AWS' deputy head Janusz Tomszewski said last week. The central bank has said the government was likely to slightly overshoot its 13 percent inflation target for December this year.
The AWS wants the bonds to generate means for creating a fund that would invest in the southern and western regions affected by the flooding, the worst in centuries.
The AWS has said it would seek to change Cimszewicz's budget draft for 1998 if it forms the next government, but would have little time to do this.
